rationale: Empirical asset-pricing paper (Moskowitz, Ooi, Pedersen 2012, JFE) documenting time series momentum in 58 liquid futures/forward contracts (24 commodities, 9 equity indexes, 13 government bonds, 12 currency pairs) from January 1965 to December 2009. Section 2 specifies data sources (Datastream, Bloomberg, exchanges, CFTC Commitments of Traders), the instrument universe (Appendix A), and the ex ante volatility model (Section 2.4). Section 3 operationalizes the strategy exactly: go long (short) if the past k-month excess return is positive (negative), size positions inversely to ex ante volatility, hold h months with Jegadeesh-Titman overlapping-cohort aggregation, and evaluate alphas against MSCI World, Barclays Aggregate, GSCI, and Fama-French SMB/HML/UMD (Eq. 4). Sections 4-6 construct the TSMOM factor (40% volatility scaling, equal-weighted across available instruments, Eq. 5), regress it on standard factors (Table 3), compare against cross-sectional momentum (Table 5), and link CFTC speculator positions to returns (Table 6). Tables 1-6 report fully operational numerical results (annualized means/volatilities, alpha t-statistics over an 8x8 look-back/holding grid, regression coefficients with t-stats). All methodology is operationalized with explicit formulas; data is futures data available in the WRDS Datastream futures database (tr_ds_fut_202606) with Fama-French factors in the ff database.
